- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) after a peak, model fails to correct; force downward adjustment by 1–3% if sentiment drops below 0.2.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 68–70 range); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights short-term momentum; reduce forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is weak or mixed (0.2–0.6) over last 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.67” patterns, model tends to ignore sentiment; apply sentiment-weighted adjustment: +0.3–0.7% for sentiment >0.5, -0.2–0.4% for sentiment <0.3.
